reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous reasoning to identify obvious shared features across instances with external XAI tools to quantify feature importance and detect spurious correlations. This ensures both pattern recognition and statistical validation of feature influence, especially for features that may appear common but lack semantic relevance to the target class.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which features are present in all three misclassified instances (13590, 2021, 26891) and list their values.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of shared features across all three instances with their corresponding values

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether any shared feature (e.g., marital-status=Married-civ-spouse, relationship=Husband) is semantically related to income class or if it could be a spurious correlate due to co-occurrence with other features.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A judgment on whether the shared feature is semantically relevant or likely spurious

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides robust, model-agnostic feature importance scores that can reveal high attribution for features not semantically linked to income. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer local interpretability to validate how features influence predictions. Sensitivity analysis confirms whether removing a feature changes the prediction, indicating spurious dependence. Together, they validate shared spurious features across misclassified instances.
